saying: Most commenters accept a graduated ladder of clinical confirmation and agree prospective studies need not always be required, but ask FDA to specify how the tier is chosen rather than leaving it to sponsor justification. Common additions: shadow deployment for intermediate risk, characterization of the anticipated real-world input distribution, subgroup and setting reporting, and evaluation of the deployed human-AI team.

disagreement.text: Commenters split on structure: some want a fixed, ordered ladder with the required tier set by risk classification (or set by FDA rather than sponsor choice), while others want the methods treated as alternative or combinable options chosen by residual uncertainty. One commenter separately opposes any waiver of prospective trials.

sides.summary: Prescribe an ordered, risk-keyed ladder with the required tier determined by FDA's risk mapping.
Treat confirmation methods as complementary or combinable options selected by residual evidentiary uncertainty, not a fixed hierarchy.
